summary: Genuine historical reconstruction of missing backlog closure metadata (closed_at/closure_repository/closure_commit/closure_evidence), no fabrication.
method: For each closed item missing fields, isolated the LAST '## Triage'/'## Resolution' section in the item's own body (items are re-triaged; only the final section reflects the real closing decision). Extracted any 'commit <sha>'/'commit: <sha>'/'Closure commit: <sha>' citation from that section and verified each candidate SHA is a real commit via `git cat-file --batch-check`. Where no explicit commit was cited but the section stated a real decision-only closure (e.g. superseded elsewhere, no code change needed, PO rejected the change), used `git log -1 -- <item file>` to find the commit that actually wrote that closing Triage section into the file -- itself a real, verifiable act of closure, matching the repo's own established convention (see backlog/evidence/2026-08-16-verify-red-suite-backlog-closures.md for the guard-testpath/semgrep precedent of citing the decision-recording commit). Every commit used was independently re-verified against `git log`/`git show` for at least a sample, and three were cross-confirmed against their own commit message's explicit 'Closes backlog items ...' list. Items whose OWN final Triage/Decision text contradicted the 'closed' frontmatter status (said 'stays open', 'accept-open', 'accept-deferred', 'Confirmed still open', etc.) were left completely untouched -- adding closure metadata to those would misrepresent a genuinely-unresolved item, which is a different, more serious problem than a metadata gap and needs a PO decision, not reconstruction.

known_residual_on_a_reconstructed_file.note: Only closure_commit was missing and has now been added (8e8dd393fd7eba110f85ecf5ce69be5f41f6bd6b, real, verified). The item's PRE-EXISTING closure_repository ('nova') and closure_evidence (a machine-specific absolute path) values were already present before this dispatch and are already schema-invalid ('closure_repository must be self or project:<slug>', 'closure_evidence must be a safe repository-relative path'); out of this dispatch's scope (only missing fields, not correcting other pre-existing fields) and left untouched per the Forbidden clause.

confirmed_unrecoverable_or_not_attempted.note: These items carry frontmatter status: closed, but their OWN final Triage/Decision text explicitly contradicts closure (says the item stays open, is deferred, or was only partially addressed). This is a status/content integrity problem, not a metadata gap -- adding fabricated-looking closure fields to an item whose own text says it is unresolved would misrepresent it. Left completely untouched; flagged for a PO decision on which is authoritative (the frontmatter status or the item's own last words).

files.own_text: Partially addressed; the item stays open, narrowed further.
partially accepted and delivered; narrowed, stays open.
partially accepted and delivered; stays open, narrowed.
accepted; a first instance of proposal step 1 already exists. Stays open -- the item's actual ask is the systematic version.
Confirmed still open and unchanged; requires the PO's three-step determination before any design or implementation work.
